For playability, I need to explicitly assign each hit to a limb (right hand, left hand, right foot, left foot), then check that no more than two hand notes and two foot notes occur at the same instant, dropping the lower-velocity ones when there's a conflict. I also want to enforce a minimum gap between consecutive hits on the same limb—around 45ms—so fast humanized offsets don't create physically impossible doubles.

I'll give each note a short fixed duration (roughly 30-40 ticks) so overlapping note-offs don't confuse a checker, computing the actual duration as the smaller of that default and the gap until the next note on the same pitch, ensuring durations never overlap into the next hit even with humanization jitter.

Since each limb's own notes stay non-overlapping this way, at most one note per hand is active at any moment, keeping simultaneous hand count at two — right hand on crash/hi-hat/toms, left on snare, kick and hi-hat pedal assigned to feet so they don't count against hand limits.

For tempo, I'll target roughly 110 BPM average over 120 seconds, which gives about 55 bars of four beats each. I'll build the sections in relative beat lengths with a tempo curve shape first, then rescale the overall base tempo afterward so the total duration lands close to 120 seconds.

For implementation, I'll set tempo per beat using tick-based positions, adding humanized offsets that convert correctly since tempo changes happen at beat boundaries. I'm laying out the arrangement in bars: a sparse 4-bar intro with a clave-like tom motif and ghost snares, then an 8-bar building groove with swung sixteenths, kick/snare accents on the motif, and hi-hat activity layered in.

I'm continuing to sketch the arrangement — hand development with paradiddles around the toms and a crescendo push, then a full-kit climax with double-bass sixteenths and crashes cutting off abruptly. After that comes a quieter contrast section using percussion like ride bell, cowbell, congas, and timbales carrying the motif, followed by a snare-roll buildup with buzz rolls and forward-leaning tempo leading into another big climax section.

I'm setting up the Python framework using mido, defining event structures for beat, note, velocity, and limb, and mapping out the General MIDI drum note numbers I'll need for the kit.

For groove feel, I want to apply swing to 16th-note offbeats based on their position within the beat, using a parameter to control swing amount per section—0 for straight, higher values for more shuffle.

I'll only apply the delay to notes landing exactly on the "e" and "a" 16th subdivisions, leaving triplets and 32nd rolls unaffected since their timing doesn't align with the swing grid, so each event needs a flag marking whether swing applies to it.

For humanization, I'm giving each limb its own timing offset in milliseconds — kick slightly ahead, snare laid back on the backbeat, hats neutral — plus a per-section push/pull feel and tiny randomized jitter, with ghost notes hitting a touch later and softer. Velocities get accents versus ghosts plus small random variation layered under a broader phrase dynamics curve. Since these offsets are in milliseconds, I need to convert them to ticks using the local tempo at that point in the track.

I'm also building a tempo curve that flexes per section — pulling back slightly in the intro, staying steady through the groove, pushing forward into the climaxes, and ritardando-ing at the very end — interpolated smoothly bar to bar, then solving for a base BPM so the whole track lands at roughly 120 seconds including the final crash's ring-out tail.

With the base tempo settled around 108bpm across ~52-53 bars, I'm now sketching the rhythmic motifs, starting with an accented 16th-note pattern for the main phrase.

I need to work out the hand assignments carefully: right hand handles continuous 16th-note hats with ghost/accent dynamics, left hand covers snare backbeats on 2 and 4 plus scattered ghost notes, while the kick partially outlines motif A, and level controls overall density. The crash cymbal takes over from the hat on beat 1, and I'm defining a tom_run function that takes a starting beat, length, subdivision, sticking pattern (like alternating or paradiddle-style strings), a path across the toms, and a velocity ramp.

Now I'm designing a roll function using alternating 32nd notes with a velocity swell for a building snare roll, plus a linear fill pattern that weaves in kick strokes. For orchestrating drum choice across a sticking pattern, I'm mapping each stroke index to a position along a list of drums so the sound moves progressively down the kit, while considering keeping the left hand anchored on snare for some patterns.

I'm defining MIDI note constants for each drum voice and grouping the toms into a list, then setting up per-bar feel data (swing amount, push timing) alongside a humanize step that adjusts each event's timing and velocity based on its bar's feel settings.

I'm setting per-instrument timing offsets—kicks slightly ahead, backbeat snares laid back, ghosts pushed later, crashes slightly ahead—then converting tempo per beat into a tick calculation for tempo events. Now I'm assembling the final MIDI, placing tempo change messages at each beat and making sure all tick values are consistent.

I need to clamp any negative ticks resulting from humanization to zero, and enforce a minimum gap between consecutive notes on the same limb by dropping the lower-velocity hit if two events fall too close together, since my construction generally keeps one limb active at a time but I want a safety check for edge cases like simultaneous same-limb hits.

I'm also thinking through note duration handling since percussion synths mostly ignore note-off and just let cymbals ring, so I can use a short fixed duration safely under the minimum gap threshold. For flams and rolls where two hands hit the same drum in close succession, overlapping note-on/note-off pairs for the same pitch should still behave fine on GM drum synths, but I want to compute durations cleanly per note to avoid any weirdness.

Now I'm setting up the actual composition structure, defining a helper function to log events with beat, note, velocity, and limb, plus a velocity humanization scheme with small random jitter and reduced variation for ghost notes.
